subject.title: fix: discord exec approvals fails against local self-signed TLS gateway

question: Should maintainers rebase/adopt the open shared-bootstrap TLS fingerprint PR as the canonical fix, or ask for a fresh narrow replacement?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and security-sensitive, but an open proof-labeled PR already owns the shared fix path and is currently conflicting, so automation should not create a duplicate fix without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt and rebase the shared PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80204 as the canonical fix path, resolve conflicts and the stale import, then rerun focused gateway/bootstrap approval validation.

options.title: Request a clean replacement
options.body: If the branch is too stale to reconcile, ask for or sponsor an equivalent narrow replacement that preserves the shared resolver scope and test coverage.

options.title: Defer the fix
options.body: Keep this issue open without another fix PR, accepting that local self-signed WSS approval/bootstrap clients remain broken.

recommendation.title: Adopt and rebase the shared PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80204 as the canonical fix path, resolve conflicts and the stale import, then rerun focused gateway/bootstrap approval validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest feature-history link to both the shared operator approval client and the existing Gateway TLS fingerprint behavior.
